div.p: 1–3 — assistant prep, on a branch 4 — the human gate 5–6 — the conversation and its processing, and 6 is 1–3 for the next round
One pull request carries both the closeout of the last conversation and the prep for the next one.
After the first turn it settles into three beats: approve → talk → process, and none of them ends with "somebody should work out what's next".

ul.li: Bold box — the gate, and the two steps the loop depends on

g.text: 1 · The machine reports what is missing — gap-analysis.py, against the records as they now stand

text.tspan: Every gap gets a name against it. Open questions · people still to be identified · what has been answered.
One per person, only for meetings that are actually coming up. The questions as you would say them
out loud, what a good answer looks like, and what NOT to ask because it is already recorded.
THE GATE. A person approves every word; the schema rejects an invented owner outright.
On merge the published docs are current AND the next brief is live and reviewed.
5 · TALK — the conversation, brief in hand
A meeting that was happening anyway. No homework for the expert: they turn up and talk. Recorded.
Records, decisions, insights, and the summary — then steps 1–3 again for the next round.

g.text: insights-surfaced.md — what the questions revealed about the organization
the rows for whoever has a meeting coming up
same pull request: closeout + next prep
